brief: New BIS export-control rules effective November 19 tighten China's access on three fronts: direct chip sales, remote access to overseas compute, and foundry-level manufacturing capability, aimed at closing the offshore compute loophole and overlapping with proposed RASA legislation. The author argues the immediate issue is licensing uncertainty freezing investment decisions, not permanent demand loss, and that this explains acute weakness in the Asian data-center trade and Chinese equities, with possible knock-on into copper and gold. This compounds pre-existing AI-multiple pressures: cost of capital (worsened by Nvidia's leadership change), DC restrictions, inference-efficiency oversupply, and insufficient revenue to support capex. Separately, SPX reversed 3.3% intraday on collapsing breadth (38 advancers, 464 decliners) and failing defensive sectors, turning rotation into outright liquidation. Fed/macro: financial conditions tightened sharply after Waller's 50bp remarks and hawkish Fed speak, evoking a November/December 2018 overtightening parallel; breakevens are collapsing while real yields sit near highs, and the long end may be pricing a policy mistake. The author favors receiving rates/owning duration, reads gold's liquidation as a real-rate signal, and sees deep de-grossing as consistent with a possible tactical local low, though no near catalyst exists before PCE, NFP and the December FOMC.
